newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto walks out of Pakistan parliament.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto walks out of Pakistan parliament.

text.p: Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto stormed out of an inaugural session of Pakistan's new parliament with her opposition party deputies on Wednesday, demanding that President Farooq Leghari step down.

Members of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) tried to interrupt Leghari's address to a joint session of the Senate (upper house) and National Assembly (lower house) by raising an uproar of objections before walking out.
However, the president, a former Bhutto protege, appeared unruffled and continued his speech, expounding the government's policies at the start of the parliamentary year.
Leghari's speech, and the opposition walkout, were shown live on state television.

Ironically, deputies from Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML), many of whom had shouted down Leghari on a similar occasion in 1994, helped him on Wednesday by cheering and thumping desks to drown out opposition protests.

Bhutto later told reporters Leghari was no longer qualified to hold office because he had engaged in corruption and nepotism and broken a pledge never to use controversial constitutional powers to sack an elected government and National Assembly.
Leghari dismissed Bhutto's three-year government on November 5 for alleged corruption and misrule and called elections on February 3, which Sharif won by a landslide.
Bhutto demanded the formation of a joint committee of both houses of parliament to inquire into her allegations.
Leghari denied the charges. "May God keep me from corruption and nepotism," he told reporters after his speech.
Leghari was PPP nominee for president when the national and provincial parliaments elected him for a six-year term in 1993.
Bhutto said he had "lost the moral justification and basis to continue in office" by dismissing components of his own electoral college.
She reiterated charges that the February 3 polls had been rigged and said the PPP was still awaiting statements of vote count at every polling station from the Election Commission.

"Leghari by his continuous conduct has shown strong bias, practiced political victimisation, interfered in holding of free, impartial and transparent elections, and displayed favouritism and nepotism in appointing his relatives and cronies to high government positions," she said.
Bhutto said Leghari had also pursued his own economic policy through an interim government he formed after sacking her.

"Subsequent events and the continued downward slide of the economic situation has clearly proved that the spurious presidential prescription for economic reforms has failed, making it thus incumbent upon him to honourably step down from his office forthwith," she declared.
